title: Robot Assembly Line Choreographer
description: The user choreographs a robot working on an assembly line of animated boxes. They assign animation speed, playback direction, and synchronization offsets to both the robot and a row of five cloned animated boxes, managing a shared 'energy budget' that conserves total animation energy across all actors. Full undo/redo support lets users experiment freely.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load robot.glb and BoxAnimated.glb via GLTFLoader. Clone BoxAnimated into 5 instances arranged in a conveyor-belt line (spaced 2 units apart along X). Place the robot at the center facing the boxes. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,4,10) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.4), a directional light from (5,10,7), and a ground plane with shadow receiving. Enable shadows on the renderer.

Core mechanic — Energy Conservation: define a total energy budget of 100 units. Each of the 6 actors (1 robot + 5 boxes) has an energy allocation (default 100/6 each). Animation timeScale for each actor equals its energy divided by a base cost of 10. When the user increases one actor's energy, all others proportionally decrease so the sum always equals 100. Display energy bars as an HTML overlay panel on the left.

Interactions (10-14 steps expected): (1-5) Click any of the 6 actors to select them — highlight with emissive outline. (6-7) Use a slider to adjust the selected actor's energy from 0-60; others auto-rebalance. (8) A 'Reverse' toggle button flips the selected actor's animation direction (negative timeScale). (9) A 'Phase Offset' slider (0-2s) shifts the selected actor's animation start time using mixer.setTime. (10) A 'Play/Pause All' button toggles global playback. (11-12) Ctrl+Z triggers undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z triggers redo — maintain a state history stack storing energy allocations, directions, and phase offsets for all actors (max 30 entries). (13) A 'Reset' button restores all defaults and clears history. (14) A 'Lock' checkbox per actor prevents its energy from being auto-rebalanced.

Play all AnimationClips from both GLBs using THREE.AnimationMixer per actor. Show the currently selected actor name and its stats in the overlay. Ensure smooth 60fps with requestAnimationFrame and delta-based mixer updates.
